sentences: Your new daily rest must be taken within 24 hours of the end of the previous one, so by 6 am the next day.
At least 9 hours of it must fall inside that 24-hour window.
That means a reduced rest has to start by 9 pm at the latest, and a full 11-hour regular rest by 7 pm.
A rest of 9 to less than 11 hours counts as a reduced daily rest, and you may take at most three reduced daily rests between any two weekly rests.
You can also split a regular daily rest into two parts: first an unbroken 3 hours or more, then an unbroken 9 hours or more.
The Commission's 2015 guidance note (older than the current act, but consistent with it) adds that your rest may run past 6 am if it is longer than the minimum.
Your next 24-hour period then starts when that rest actually ends.

sentences: A 'driving period' is all the driving you add up from when you start driving after a rest period or a break until you next take a rest period or a break.
It can be continuous or broken up.
After a driving period of 4.5 hours you must take an uninterrupted break of at least 45 minutes, unless you take a rest period instead.
You may split this break into at least 15 minutes followed by at least 30 minutes.
If you drive an occasional passenger service, you may instead take two breaks of at least 15 minutes each, spread over the driving period.
In multi-manning, you can take the 45-minute break in the moving vehicle while the other driver drives, as long as you are not helping that driver.
During any break you may not drive or do any other work; it is only for recuperation.

sentences: Night work does not change the break rules.
You must never work more than six hours in a row without a break.
If your working hours total more than nine hours, you need breaks of at least 45 minutes in total; if they total between six and nine hours, at least 30 minutes.
Night work matters in a different way: when you do night work, your daily working time must not exceed ten hours in each 24-hour period.
Breaks are not counted as working time.
So the night-work limit allows up to 10 hours of actual work, plus at least 45 minutes of breaks on top, with no stretch longer than six hours.
Night time is a period of at least four hours between 00.00 and 07.00, as set by national law.

During it you need not stay at your workstation, but you must be ready to start or resume driving or do other work.

On the tachograph, after crossing into another Member State you must enter the symbol of the country you have entered.
Do this at the start of your first stop there, which must be at the nearest possible stopping place at or after the border.
If you cross by ferry or train, enter it at the port or station of arrival.

You do not have to if the tachograph records location data automatically.

sentences: Yes.
A driver doing international goods transport may take two reduced weekly rests in a row (each at least 24 hours) while outside the Member State where the employer is established.

(2) In any four consecutive weeks you must take at least four weekly rests, and at least two of them must be regular rests of at least 45 hours.
(3) Both reductions must be made up with an equivalent rest taken in one block.

sentences: Usually no.
Under the current Regulation, the EU driving time rules do not apply to a vehicle of up to 7,5 tonnes that carries materials, equipment or machinery for your own use in your work.

Your 6-tonne truck carrying your tools qualifies, but only if three conditions are met: you stay within 100 km of your company's base, driving is not your main activity, and the transport is not done for hire or reward.
Building sites up to 80 km away are inside that limit, so as a carpenter carrying your own tools you are exempt.
If you drive further than 100 km, carry goods for others for payment, or driving becomes your main job, the rules apply, for example the 9-hour daily driving limit.
An older Commission note from 2007 describes a 50 km limit and says each Member State decides whether to grant this exemption.
That note predates the 2020 changes.
The current Regulation sets 100 km and makes the exclusion part of the Regulation itself.

Any driver may split it into at least 15 minutes followed by at least 30 minutes.
Because you drive an occasional passenger service, you may instead replace it with two breaks of at least 15 minutes each.
